text:
Alex (AE): Heads up — procurement at ACME flagged a mismatch on AWS Marketplace invoices for the POC. They insist the invoice needs to show 'ACME Corp' as the vendor remittance entity. POC needs to start next week. @Maria - any quick options?
Maria - Finance: AWS Marketplace invoices are issued by AWS and typically show AWS as the biller. We can't change that on the invoice. Questions: do they need vendor name on the invoice or tax ID / remit address? That determines workaround.
Katy Procurement: They require vendor name + remit-to address + W9 (US) or VAT ID. Their AP won't accept invoices that don't match vendor name on their supplier list. Options: 1) Do the sale off-marketplace and issue a Redwood invoice, 2) Customer accepts AWS invoice (unlikely for them). They prefer #1.
Jordan - Deals: Moving off-marketplace will break marketplace commit tracking and some channel discounts. Can we do a direct invoice for the POC and keep marketplace for future committed buys? Need deal-desk sign-off. @Sarah - Deal Desk can you weigh in?
Sarah - Deal Desk: We can approve a one-off direct quote for POCs < $10k at marketplace-equivalent pricing without exec sign-off. Commits and reserved capacity must be handled by contract later. Need expected dollar amount and invoice terms.
Alex (AE): POC estimated at ~$8k (1 month). Customer says their procurement only allows purchases through marketplace because of preferred vendor list — they can't add new vendors easily. So they actually want marketplace billing but with Redwood listed as vendor remittance. Any hack?
Maria - Finance: No clean way to change AWS invoice biller. Possible but high-friction workaround: issue a Redwood self-bill or credit memo referencing the AWS invoice, but that requires legal + finance approvals and could delay payment.
billing-bot: Automated ticket created: FIN-2026-78 to evaluate marketplace-pass-through and vendor remittance options. Assigned to maria.finance.
Katy Procurement: If we provide a signed supplier form (legal name, EIN, remit address) some customers will accept that alongside the AWS invoice and release payment. Problem: AP requires PO number on invoice; AWS invoices don't include customer PO in a way their systems match.
Maria - Finance: We can provide supplier paperwork and a vendor addendum, but if AP's ERP requires PO -> invoice match, they'll need to accept a direct Redwood invoice. Otherwise payments may be held.
Jordan - Deals: Proposed approach: run POC on a short, direct Redwood invoice (one-time Net30), and plan for future committed purchases through marketplace. Ask customer to do a one-time marketplace card purchase for a token item if they must have a marketplace transaction for internal records. I'll coordinate with procurement. @Katy Procurement can you escalate if needed?
Katy Procurement: I can escalate to their AP. If they insist on marketplace on-card purchase, a small marketplace transaction + a direct Redwood invoice for the POC is a practical compromise. They'll need the supplier form from us.
Alex (AE): I'll tell the customer that route. @Sarah - can you draft a one-off quote that mirrors marketplace pricing and terms (Net30) so procurement can approve?
Sarah - Deal Desk: On it. Drafting a one-off quote at marketplace-equivalent pricing. We can approve within 5% of marketplace list for <$10k. Expect a PDF by EOD. No commit discounts for this POC.
Jordan - Deals: Note for tracking: do NOT apply commit discounts until legal signs committed contract. POC quote must be explicitly non-binding.
Alex (AE): Understood. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Alex (AE): Example of the quote I'll send to buyer:
```
Item | Qty | Price
Redwood Inference - POC | 1 | $8,000.00
Terms: Net30, one-time, no commit discount
```

Maria - Finance: I'll attach supplier paperwork (W9 + vendor profile) to the ticket FIN-2026-78. If AP refuses, we'll escalate to finance leadership.
Katy Procurement: I'll follow up with buyer's AP contact and confirm whether token marketplace purchase + Redwood invoice is acceptable.
Alex (AE): Perfect. Will update customer and loop anyone needed.
Sarah - Deal Desk: Quote uploaded to SFDC and linked in the ticket. If finance/legal needs to review anything beyond standard terms I will ping you.
Jordan - Deals: Closing note: label this POC as 'marketplace-equivalent' in CRM to keep handoff clean when we convert to committed business.
Alex (AE): Thanks all, closing the loop here.
